observations:
Torah LM2:41 is among the shortest in the entire corpus — three sentences with a single cohesive argument. The bechina topology is minimal: one cluster of concepts all belonging to the domain of divine miracle-working through the posek's authority.

The teaching's structure:
- 'מוֹפְתִים' (miracles) ←bechina→ 'מִשְׁפְּטֵי פִיהוּ' (rulings of the posek's mouth): the verse from I Chronicles 16:12 is brought via 'בִּבְחִינַת' to establish that the posek's ruling and the divine wonder are the same thing.
- 'מוֹפְתֵי הַגְּאוֹנִים' ←bechina→ the same phenomenon: the closing line uses 'וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת' to confirm that the historical miracles of the Geonim belong to this same domain.
- 'בַּעֲלֵי הַפּוֹסְקִים' and the Geonim are bechina-equivalent figures: both are the authoritative halachic voice through which divine will manifests.

All concepts in the source text converge into a single package (Package 1: מוֹפְתִים וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי פֶּה). There is no second independent domain, no evil counterpart, and no structural/neutral cluster separate from the main teaching.

Candidate reviewed and rejected: One might consider separating 'קַבָּלַת הַפְּסַק' (the community's acceptance of the posek's authority) into its own neutral or structural package, since it is the mechanism that enables the miracle. However, the Rebbe does not use bechina language for this concept — it is presented as the explanatory mechanism (eitza: because his authority is accepted, miracles flow through him). This is cause-and-effect reasoning internal to the explanation, not a second bechina domain. It does not qualify for its own package.

Conclusion: The single package (מוֹפְתִים וּמִשְׁפְּטֵי פֶּה) fully covers the bechina topology of LM2:41. No new packages are warranted.
